xref.title: Birth (1942)
xref.body: James Paul McCartney was born on June 18, 1942, to Jim and Mary McCartney. His parents met and married on April 15, 1941, under circumstances heavily influenced by World War II, including his father's exemption from military service due to a childhood ear injury and an air raid in Liverpool. "Then on June 18, 1942, they had a son. They named him James Paul McCartney."

xref.title: Paul McCartney's Birth (1942)
xref.body: Paul McCartney was born on June 18, 1942, to Jim and Mary McCartney, whose meeting and marriage on April 15, 1941, was an indirect consequence of World War II. Jim McCartney's exemption from military service due to a childhood ear injury (from falling off a wall in 1912) and the timing of a German Luftwaffe bombing raid in Liverpool in 1941, which led him to his mother's place where Mary was visiting, are cited as critical events leading to their union and Paul's birth. "Then on June 18, 1942, they had a son. They named him James Paul McCartney."

xref.title: Dave Grohl's Father Covered the Kent State Massacre (May 1970)
xref.body: In 1970, the Grohl family lived in Niles, Ohio (near Columbus). Dave's father James Grohl was a reporter for the Scripps News Agency and was assigned to cover anti-Vietnam War protests at Kent State University on May 1, 1970 — and was present when the National Guard opened fire, killing four students. James Grohl won several awards for his on-the-spot reporting, earning a major promotion and reassignment to Washington D.C., where Dave grew up and discovered music. "Had it not been for the National Guard killing four unarmed students at Kent State, who knows if we'd ever have heard of Dave Grohl?"

xref.title: Columbus Holiday Inn Bar Fight (March 10, 1979) – Racist Remarks, Punch from Bonnie Bramlett, Career Nearly Ruined in America
xref.body: On March 10, 1979, Elvis Costello and his entourage were drinking heavily in a bar at a Holiday Inn in Columbus, Ohio, when they encountered Stephen Stills's party. Costello made blatant racist remarks about Ray Charles and James Brown. Stephen Stills's companion Bonnie Bramlett punched Costello, a full brawl broke out, and the incident made national news. American media sided with Stills; Costello became toxic and his American career took years to recover. He later described the incident in his memoirs *Unfaithful Music and Disappearing Ink* (2015) and acknowledged it without denial or excuse. "An old barfight from 37 years ago — but there are real serious things that haven't been fixed that are not my doing or my responsibility."

xref.body: Tapeworm was conceived as a side project during Nine Inch Nails' "The Downward Spiral" sessions in 1994, intended as a collaborative effort for Danny Lohner and Charlie Clouser. It evolved to include a star-studded lineup: Trent Reznor, Maynard James Keenan (Tool), producer Alan Molder, Atticus Ross, Phil Anselmo and Rex Brown (Pantera), Page Hamilton (Helmet), Toni Halliday (Curve), Tommy Victor (Ministry), and drummer Josh Freese, with at least an album's worth of material recorded by 2001. "If you're Trent Rezner, Danny Loaner and Charlie Closer from his live band, Maynard James Keenan from Tool, producer Alan Molder and Atticus Ross. I mean, wow, awesome, right? The idea for tapeworm went as far back as the sessions for the downward spiral in 1994. Tapeworm was designed as something to which Danny and Charlie could contribute as equals. This idea evolved into something pretty cool. Maynard was brought in, Phil and Salmo from Pantera, Paige Hamilton from Helmut, Tony Haliday from a cool band called Curve, Tommy Victor from Ministry, drummer Josh Freeze. xref.title: Disappearance from Embassy Hotel (February 1, 1995)
xref.body: Richey Edwards walked out of room 516 of the Embassy Hotel on Bayswater Road in London at 7:00 am on February 1, 1995, and disappeared forever, the day he was supposed to fly to the US for a promo tour with bandmate James Dean Bradfield. Leading up to his disappearance, he had withdrawn £200 daily for two weeks, accumulating nearly £3,000 in cash. He left behind a packed suitcase, toiletries, a bottle of Prozac, and a carefully wrapped box for a 19-year-old female friend with a note that said, "I love you." His car was found abandoned at a service station two weeks later, suggesting someone had been living in it. He was officially presumed dead in November 2008, and his disappearance remains one of modern Britain's greatest missing person mysteries. "On February 1st, 1995... he walked out of the hotel at 7 in the morning and disappeared forever."

xref.title: Richie Edwards' Disappearance (1995)
xref.body: Richie Edwards, an extreme member of the Manic Street Preachers known for depression, anorexia, drug use, and self-mutilation, disappeared on February 1, 1995, following the death of his dog on January 14, 1995. xref.title: Jimmy Chamberlain's Firing and Return (1996-1999)
xref.body: Five days after Jonathan Melvoin's death, Billy, James, and Darcy of The Smashing Pumpkins issued a statement announcing their decision to "sever our relationship with our friend and drummer Jimmy Chamberlain." They explained that for nine years they had "battled with Jimmy's struggles with the insidious disease of drug and alcohol addiction," which had "nearly destroyed everything we are and stand for," and confirmed they would "carry on without him." Jimmy was exiled from the band for three years, a period during which the Pumpkins' fortunes began to decline. In an effort to revitalize the band, Jimmy was eventually asked to rejoin, making his return on April 10, 1999, at St Andrews Hall in Detroit, where the band appeared in their familiar lineup for the first time since July 1996. "Today, we are very sorry to tell you that we've decided to sever our relationship with our friend and drummer Jimmy Chamberlain."

xref.title: Tom Verlaine Death (January 28, 2023) – Prostate Cancer, Age 73; Helped CBGB Become Ground Zero for Punk
xref.body: Tom Verlaine co-founded Television and in 1973 helped Hilly Kristal — owner of a scuzzy bar on Bleecker Street in a then-terrible part of New York — to let Television play a Sunday night residency. This decision catalyzed CBGB into becoming ground zero for New York punk and, by chain reaction, the entire international punk movement. Television produced two critically acclaimed albums before breaking up in 1978. Verlaine subsequently collaborated with Patti Smith, worked with James Iha of the Smashing Pumpkins, had a song covered by David Bowie, and was involved in a 1992 Television reunion album. He was scheduled to produce Jeff Buckley's second album — a project ended when Buckley drowned in the Mississippi River in 1997. Verlaine was diagnosed with prostate cancer at some point in the 2000s; it metastasized. He died January 28, 2023, age 73. "That was the catalyst for making CBGB ground zero for the world of New York punk."

xref.title: Mid-60s Garage Band
xref.body: The Seeds were identified as one of several rough, ragged, and raw-sounding bands from the 1960s. Originating from garages and basements across North America, these groups often adopted a tough aesthetic, including leather jackets, which some people associated with a "rebellious Marlon Brando or James Dean kind of look," leading to them being perceived as "punks." "There were the seeds."

xref.title: Riff Origin Anecdote
xref.body: Jack White spontaneously created the signature seven-note riff for "Seven Nation Army" during a soundcheck on January 29, 2002, at the Corner Hotel in Melbourne, Australia. He found the riff "cool" and played it repeatedly, even though Ben Swank from Third Man Records initially disliked it and suggested Jack "can do better." White even considered it for a James Bond theme before deciding to use it for a White Stripes song. "Jack White came up with a seven note riff, which he thought sounded cool, so he played it over and over and over again."

xref.title: Suicide Runs in Kurt Cobain's Family Across Multiple Generations
xref.body: Kurt's great-great-grandfather John Cobain was a county sheriff who accidentally shot himself in 1938. His great-grandfather James Irving stabbed himself in the stomach in front of his family in 1935, was institutionalized, and died two months later after ripping out his own stitches. His great-uncle Burl Cobain shot himself in the stomach with a .38 in 1979; when that failed he shot himself in the head. At age 14, Kurt told friends he planned to kill himself one day after becoming a rock star. At 15 he and his stepbrother James made a short film called *Kurt Commits Bloody Suicide*. At 13 he wrote in his journals of planning to actually kill himself. At 16, drunk and stoned, he lay on train tracks with a large piece of cement on his chest waiting to be hit; the train went past on a different track. The famous March 1994 Rome hotel overdose was the last major attempt before his death on April 5, 1994 (aged 27) in his Seattle home. "He said he had suicide genes."
